The task: estimate software development effort for porting modules from Spring XD to spring-cloud-stream (s-c-s) repo, based on user stories U1-U8.

Modules to port:
- U1: router module (sink)
- U2: file module (sink)
- U3: FTP module (sink)
- U4: redis module (sink)
- U5: rabbit module (source)
- U6: gemfire module (sink)
- U7: upgrade HDP/PHD distros for HDFS support
- U8: documentation section on migration strategy 1.2 -> 1.3

I need to produce WBS with activities, each with most likely effort in work-hours, and total.

Let me think of a reasonable breakdown:

Per module porting (each has similar structure):
1. Analysis of existing XD module code and design adaptation to spring-cloud-stream programming model
2. Code port/implementation (module adapter, auto-configuration, binder integration)
3. Configuration properties/metadata
4. Unit tests
5. Integration tests
6. Build/CI integration (Maven/Gradle, repo setup)
7. Code review & rework
8. Documentation (README, reference docs)

Plus cross-cutting:
- Project setup/infrastructure for new modules in s-c-s repo
- U7: HDP/PHD distro upgrade: update dependencies, test HDFS integration
- U8: Migration documentation 1.2->1.3
- Overall integration/release validation

Estimates: These are historical real tasks from spring-cloud-stream-modules repo. Let me assign reasonable hours.

Simple modules (router, file, ftp, redis, rabbit, gemfire) — each maybe 40-80 hours total including tests and docs.

Let me create activity breakdown per module with sub-activities, or aggregate per module? WBS-based: break down into activities necessary to deliver. I'll produce activities grouped:

A1: Project setup and repository/build infrastructure — 16h
Per module (6 modules): analysis/design 4-8h, implementation 16-24h, unit tests 8-12h, integration tests 8-12h, docs 4h, review/rework 4h. Each module ~44-64h.

U7: HDP/PHD upgrade: dependency analysis 8h, implementation/upgrade 16h, testing 16h → 40h.

U8: Migration docs: 16-24h.

Final integration & release validation: 16h.

Let me make concrete numbers:

Common:
- A1: Repository & build setup (Maven modules, CI, checkstyle, BOM integration): 16h

U1 Router sink (router uses SpEL / groovy router):
- A2: Analysis & design: 6h
- A3: Implementation: 20h (router needs dynamic routing, script support)
- A4: Unit tests: 10h
- A5: Integration tests: 10h
- A6: Docs: 4h
- A7: Review/rework: 6h
Subtotal: 56h

U2 File sink:
- A8: Analysis: 4h
- A9: Implementation: 16h
- A10: Unit tests: 8h
- A11: Integration tests: 8h
- A12: Docs: 4h
- A13: Review/rework: 4h
Subtotal: 44h

U3 FTP sink:
- A14: Analysis: 4h
- A15: Implementation: 18h
- A16: Unit tests: 8h
- A17: Integration tests (embedded FTP server): 10h
- A18: Docs: 4h
- A19: Review/rework: 4h
Subtotal: 48h

U4 Redis sink:
- A20: Analysis: 4h
- A21: Implementation: 14h
- A22: Unit tests: 8h
- A23: Integration tests (embedded redis): 8h
- A24: Docs: 4h
- A25: Review/rework: 4h
Subtotal: 42h

U5 Rabbit source:
- A26: Analysis: 4h
- A27: Implementation: 14h
- A28: Unit tests: 8h
- A29: Integration tests (rabbit broker required): 10h
- A30: Docs: 4h
- A31: Review/rework: 4h
Subtotal: 44h

U6 Gemfire sink:
- A32: Analysis: 6h
- A33: Implementation: 18h
- A34: Unit tests: 8h
- A35: Integration tests: 12h
- A36: Docs: 4h
- A37: Review/rework: 4h
Subtotal: 52h

U7 HDP/PHD upgrade:
- A38: Research/dependency analysis: 8h
- A39: Implement distro version upgrades: 12h
- A40: HDFS integration testing: 16h
- A41: Docs update: 4h
Subtotal: 40h

U8 Migration doc 1.2->1.3:
- A42: Gather changes/incompatibilities: 8h
- A43: Write migration section: 12h
- A44: Review/publish: 4h
Subtotal: 24h

Cross-cutting:
- A45: Final integration validation & release readiness: 16h

Total: 16 + 56 + 44 + 48 + 42 + 44 + 52 + 40 + 24 + 16 = let me compute: 16+56=72; +44=116; +48=164; +42=206; +44=250; +52=302; +40=342; +24=366; +16=382.

Total 382 work-hours.

Assumptions: developer familiar with Spring XD and spring-cloud-stream; existing XD module source available; s-c-s repo build infrastructure exists but needs extension; effort excludes elapsed calendar time; includes unit/integration testing, docs, code review rework; excludes project management overhead beyond review; test infrastructure (embedded brokers/servers) available; HDP/PHD distro versions specified (latest releases at time); no clarifications.

Technical decisions: port as Spring Boot auto-configured modules using spring-cloud-stream binder model; use Spring Integration adapters where XD modules already used them; configuration via @ConfigurationProperties; tests with JUnit, embedded servers (SSHD for FTP, embedded Redis, RabbitMQ test broker or Qpid? rabbit needs actual broker—use embedded/test rule); Gradle/Maven build per module as separate repos under spring-cloud-stream-modules.

technical_and_design_decisions: Port each XD module as a standalone Spring Boot application following the spring-cloud-stream (s-c-s) programming model, with a @EnableBinding-based Sink/Source interface instead of the XD module transport abstractions.

Reuse the existing Spring Integration channel adapters and handlers already underpinning the XD modules (router, file, FTP, Redis, RabbitMQ, GemFire) to minimize rewriting of core message-handling logic.
Expose module configuration through @ConfigurationProperties classes following s-c-s naming conventions, replacing XD module option metadata.
Organize each ported module as its own Maven module in the s-c-s repo (app-starters style: core module plus generated app), wired into the parent build and CI.

Implement unit tests with JUnit/Mockito and integration tests using embedded/test infrastructure: embedded SFTP/FTP server (Apache Mina/SSHD), embedded Redis, a RabbitMQ test broker, and an in-process GemFire cache.
For U7, upgrade the Hadoop distro dependencies (HDP/PHD) to the latest stable releases available and validate HDFS-related modules against them.
For U8, add the migration section to the existing Asciidoc reference documentation, covering new features and backward-incompatible changes between 1.2 and 1.3.
assumptions: The developer performing the work is experienced with Spring XD, Spring Integration, Spring Boot, and spring-cloud-stream, so no significant ramp-up time is required.
Full source code of the Spring XD modules to be ported is available and buildable.
The s-c-s repository, parent build, BOM, and CI infrastructure already exist; only extension for the new modules is needed.
Each ported module targets a single role (sink or source) as stated in the user stories; no additional processor variants are required.
Integration test infrastructure (embedded servers, local RabbitMQ broker availability, Hadoop test cluster or mini-cluster for HDFS) is available without licensing or procurement delays.

Estimates include analysis, design adaptation, implementation, unit and integration testing, documentation, and code-review rework; they exclude project management, release orchestration beyond a final validation pass, and elapsed calendar time (waiting on reviews/CI queues is counted only as active effort).
For U7, 'latest releases of HDP/PHD' means the latest stable distro versions available at the time of the work, with compatible Spring for Apache Hadoop / Spring XD Hadoop support libraries.
Code review is performed by a peer whose time is not counted; only the author's rework time is included.

activities.activity_description: Create new Maven module skeletons in the s-c-s repo for the six ported modules, wire them into the parent build/BOM, configure CI jobs, code style checks, and app-starter generation.

activities.activity_name: Router sink - analysis and design adaptation
activities.activity_description: U1: Analyze the XD router module (SpEL/Groovy-based routing) and design its adaptation to the s-c-s sink model, including dynamic destination resolution approach.
U1: Port the router module code to an s-c-s sink, including configuration properties, routing expression handling, and script support.
U1: Write unit tests for routing logic, expression evaluation, and configuration property binding.
U1: Write integration tests running the router sink against a test binder with various routing expressions and scripts.
U1: Write README and reference documentation describing options and usage of the router sink.
U1: Address code review feedback and finalize the router sink module.

activities.activity_name: File sink - analysis and design adaptation
activities.activity_description: U2: Analyze the XD file module and design its adaptation to the s-c-s sink model (directory, filename generation, append/replace modes).
U2: Port the file module code to an s-c-s sink using the Spring Integration file outbound adapter with s-c-s configuration properties.
U2: Write unit tests for filename expression handling, write modes, and property binding.
U2: Write integration tests writing messages to the local filesystem via the test binder.
U2: Write README and reference documentation for the file sink.
U2: Address code review feedback and finalize the file sink module.

activities.activity_name: FTP sink - analysis and design adaptation
activities.activity_description: U3: Analyze the XD FTP module and design its adaptation to the s-c-s sink model, including session factory configuration and remote filename handling.
U3: Port the FTP module code to an s-c-s sink using the Spring Integration FTP outbound adapter with connection and transfer configuration properties.
U3: Write unit tests for configuration properties, remote path/filename expression handling, and transfer options.
U3: Write integration tests against an embedded FTP server validating end-to-end file transfer.
U3: Write README and reference documentation for the FTP sink.
U3: Address code review feedback and finalize the FTP sink module.

activities.activity_name: Redis sink - analysis and design adaptation
activities.activity_description: U4: Analyze the XD redis module and design its adaptation to the s-c-s sink model, including key/topic expression and data structure options.
U4: Port the redis module code to an s-c-s sink using the Spring Integration Redis outbound adapter and Spring Data Redis configuration.
U4: Write unit tests for key expression handling, property binding, and payload conversion.
U4: Write integration tests against an embedded Redis server validating writes for supported data structures.
U4: Write README and reference documentation for the redis sink.
U4: Address code review feedback and finalize the redis sink module.

activities.activity_name: Rabbit source - analysis and design adaptation
activities.activity_description: U5: Analyze the XD rabbit module and design its adaptation to the s-c-s source model, including queue, exchange, and acknowledgement configuration.
U5: Port the rabbit module code to an s-c-s source using the Spring Integration AMQP inbound adapter with connection and listener configuration properties.
U5: Write unit tests for configuration property binding and message conversion behavior.
U5: Write integration tests against a RabbitMQ test broker validating message consumption end to end.
U5: Write README and reference documentation for the rabbit source.
U5: Address code review feedback and finalize the rabbit source module.

activities.activity_name: GemFire sink - analysis and design adaptation
activities.activity_description: U6: Analyze the XD gemfire module and design its adaptation to the s-c-s sink model, including region, key expression, and cache client configuration.
U6: Port the gemfire module code to an s-c-s sink using Spring Data GemFire with region and client-cache configuration properties.
U6: Write unit tests for key expression evaluation, property binding, and payload serialization.
U6: Write integration tests using an in-process GemFire cache validating region writes end to end.
U6: Write README and reference documentation for the gemfire sink.
U6: Address code review feedback and finalize the gemfire sink module.

activities.activity_name: HDP/PHD upgrade - research and dependency analysis
activities.activity_description: U7: Identify the latest stable HDP and PHD distro releases, analyze compatibility of Hadoop client libraries and Spring for Apache Hadoop support, and plan the upgrade.

activities.activity_name: HDP/PHD upgrade - dependency and code changes
activities.activity_description: U7: Update distro dependency versions, profiles, and any code or configuration affected by API changes.
U7: Validate HDFS-related pipelines against the upgraded distros using a Hadoop test cluster/mini-cluster, and fix issues found.
U7: Update documentation to reflect supported HDP/PHD distro versions and any usage changes.
U8: Collect and verify the list of new improvements and backward-incompatible changes between the 1.2 and 1.3 releases from changelogs, issues, and module changes.
U8: Write the migration strategy section in the reference documentation, covering improvements, incompatibilities, and recommended migration steps.
U8: Incorporate documentation review feedback and publish the migration section as part of the reference docs build.

activities.activity_name: Final integration validation and release readiness
activities.activity_description: Run a final cross-module build and integration validation pass (all six ported modules plus HDFS-related modules), verify CI is green, resolve remaining issues, and confirm the increment is release-ready.
